steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Place pie pastry into a 9-inch pie pan; line with a double layer of aluminum foil and a layer of pie weights or dried beans.

Bake in the preheated oven until golden on the edges, about 8 minutes. Carefully remove the foil and weights; continue baking until crust is set and dry, about 5 minutes more. Remove from the oven and reduce the temperature to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

While the crust is baking, cook bacon in a large skillet over medium-high heat until crisp, about 10 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate and crumble when cool enough to handle. Drain all but 2 tablespoons drippings from the skillet.
Add onion to drippings in the skillet; cook and stir over medium heat until tender, about 5 minutes. Use a slotted spoon and transfer to a bowl.
Toss Swiss cheese and flour together in a small bowl. Whisk milk, eggs, and salt together in a large bowl, then stir in bacon and onion.
Mix in cheese mixture until well combined, then pour into pie crust.
Bake in the preheated oven until a knife inserted into the center comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes. Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple Quiche Lorraine
raw_recipe.description: Make this easy quiche Lorraine featuring eggs, bacon, onion, and Swiss cheese baked in a store-bought crust, and serve it for any meal of the day!

review.reviewBody: This quiche was very easy to make and tasted great. I used cheddar cheese because I don't like swiss cheese and I added a small amount of black pepper to the mixture before cooking.

I made this recipe exactly as written for a wedding shower, except I made mini-quiches in muffin pans (using Pillsbury prepared pie crust cut into 4" circles). I put foil over the crust to keep it from getting too brown. I was able to get 14 mini's from the recipe. Everyone at the shower wanted the recipe!

Great recipe! Used heavy cream instead of milk and bacon bits instead of cooking bacon. Threw bits in with onions and sautéed them. Added 3/4 cup fresh shredded white cheddar and 3/4 cup Italian mix. Definitely a keeper!

What a great, simple, starter quiche. I followed the recipe but just added things. I chopped onion and added chopped bell pepper and a small amount of celery. I sautéed all that in a little olive oil; then drained them on a paper towel before adding. I cut down one small bunch of broccoli into tiny florets. You could add any veggies and/or meats you like. For seasoning, I added a heavy dash of nutmeg, smoked paprika; a touch of cayenne and black peppers. This is just one of those recipes that you can customize differently every time. I am so grateful to have the amounts for eggs, milk, cheese, etc. and bake times and temps.

I have used this recipe many times. It is better than the recipe made for the wealthy that I cooked for. Its simple, its easy and so flavorful. To make it quicker, if in a hurry, use pre cooked bacon. Tastes just as good and is ready in a snap. Its my go to for dinner and when people drop in. It is ready before you can finish a conversation. I would recommend this to anyone and already have. Its a breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner miraculous meal. Serve anytime. You can change it it to ham and cheddar or broccoli and cheddar and ham. The possibilities are endless. "All recipes," is my place to turn to when I need a quick and delicious meal. Thank you all recipes. You are the greatest.

I made this recipe Quiche Lorraine II.
I used to cups of leftover ham from Easter, 1 onion, chopped; red & green peppers, and 1 cup of Cut broccoli.....
used 3 eggs, 1 1/3 cups of 2 @% milk, the salt,
1 1/2 cups of shredded cheese and flour.

I cooked the ham, onions, red & green peppers, together w/ tsp. oil. Cooked some broccoli.....
Do my pie shell then when cooled, add the chopped broccoli. Then add the 3 eggs, the milk, and salt. Mix well. then I added the cheddar cheese, and the tbsp of flour mix well again. Then the meat and vegetables put in oven and baked at 325F for 35 to 40 minutes and everyone loved it.
So this recipe is a saver for our family. 
Thank you ALLrecipes for such a delicious recipe.
Hugs. grannyfrye

I accidentally popped the onions into the eggs before I realized I should have sauteed them. I cut the milk down by 1/2 cup and added one egg. It turned out perfectly and everyone ate every single bite. It would have been even better if I'd sauteed the onions, but I had used Microwaveable Already cooked bacon (to keep the prep and cleanup easier). I'll definitely make this again!

To everyone who thought it was missing something---it is. Nutmeg. A French reviewer noted on this site that you're supposed to add "muscade" but she didn't know what that was called in English. It's nutmeg. About 1/4 tsp adds a lot. A combo of leeks and onions is better than just onions. Also add about 1/2 tsp white pepper, and don't add the salt if you're using smoked bacon, which is usually salty enough. Use half & half for a better texture, and feel free to use Gruyere cheese, or to mix Swiss and Gruyere. You may need to cook longer than stated, up to about an hour to firm up the filling. The colder the quiche going into the oven, the longer the bake time, so I leave everything out to room temperature and it bakes in about 45 mns. The low temperature is a must because the eggs are meant to cook slow and low.
I adjusted a few thin gs. . . Four eggs instead of three; half an onion instead of a whole; mozzarella crust instead of pastry. I love it.
Made this several times. Always turns out great! Thanks to COVID I was out of onion so substituted a can of green chili’s. Ran out of Swiss so I used cheddar. Still turned out wonderful!
I added Heavy whipping cream instead of the milk and 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms to make this great, This came out awesome!!
Very easy recipe for a quiche. I added pepper to the mix because I love pepper! Love the taste of the sauteed onions in the mix too. My husband loves quiche and ate half of the quiche! Thank you
I used cheddar cheese since I didn’t have Swiss but it was still great. And very easy to make.
This quiche was so easy to make and tasted great!

Flavors great and everything. One note: I it might be helpful to know that this recipe is too big for a store-bought crust in a pan. The author must be referring to a store bought crust that you roll out. Wish I would have just made a crust really quick.
I added spinach and one more egg. Almost too much volume, but it worked. So yummy and easy!! Family loves it!!
I love this recipe ,I going to use this offen. Thank you for sharing.
Delicious as is or add a little nutmeg like the French do. I think the nutmeg adds a little more flavor.
